title: Tor & Dark Web Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete security checklist for using Tor browser and accessing the dark web safely. Essential privacy tips for anonymous browsing and protection.
intro: Using Tor and accessing the dark web requires careful security practices to maintain anonymity and protect your privacy. This comprehensive checklist covers essential steps for safe Tor usage, from initial setup to ongoing security measures.

items.task: Download Tor Browser from official source only
items.why: Fake Tor browsers contain malware and compromise your anonymity from the start.
items.howTo: Visit torproject.org directly, verify SSL certificate, and download from official links. Never use third-party sites or app stores.

items.task: Verify Tor Browser signature before installation
items.why: Ensures the downloaded file hasn't been tampered with by malicious actors.
items.howTo: Download the signature file from Tor Project, use GPG to verify authenticity. Instructions are provided on the official download page.

items.task: Set Tor Browser security level to Safest
items.why: Disables JavaScript and other features that can leak your real IP address.
items.howTo: Click the shield icon in Tor Browser, select 'Advanced Security Settings', choose 'Safest' level.

items.task: Enable automatic Tor Browser updates
items.why: Keeps you protected against newly discovered vulnerabilities and security flaws.
items.howTo: Go to Settings > General > Updates, select 'Automatically install updates (recommended)'.

items.task: Configure bridge relays if in censored country
items.why: Helps bypass ISP blocking and government censorship of Tor traffic.
items.howTo: In Tor Browser settings, go to Connection, enable bridges. Request bridges from bridges@torproject.org or use built-in options.

items.task: Enable circuit display to monitor connection path
items.why: Allows you to see which relays your traffic passes through for transparency.
items.howTo: Click the 'i' icon in address bar to view current circuit. Familiarize yourself with relay locations.

items.task: Keep JavaScript disabled at all times
items.why: JavaScript can execute code that reveals your real IP address and fingerprints your browser.
items.howTo: Maintain 'Safest' security level. Never enable JavaScript even for trusted sites while using Tor.

items.task: Avoid downloading files through Tor
items.why: Downloaded files may contain malware or tracking mechanisms that bypass Tor protection.
items.howTo: If absolutely necessary, download to isolated system, scan with antivirus, and never open files while Tor is running.

items.task: Only visit HTTPS websites and.onion sites
items.why: HTTP traffic can be monitored by exit nodes, compromising your privacy and security.
items.howTo: Look for the lock icon in address bar. Use HTTPS Everywhere extension (built into Tor Browser) to force HTTPS connections.

items.task: Never log into personal accounts through Tor
items.why: Logging into personal accounts defeats the purpose of anonymity and links your identity to Tor usage.
items.howTo: Create separate, anonymous accounts if needed. Never access email, social media, or banking through Tor.

items.task: Use 'New Identity' feature regularly
items.why: Changes your circuit and clears cookies to prevent tracking across browsing sessions.
items.howTo: Click hamburger menu > New Identity, or use Ctrl+Shift+L. Do this every 15-30 minutes or when changing topics.

items.task: Keep browser window at default size
items.why: Unique window sizes can be used to fingerprint and identify your browser session.
items.howTo: Don't maximize or resize Tor Browser window. Use the default size that opens automatically.

items.task: Consider using VPN before connecting to Tor
items.why: Hides Tor usage from your ISP and adds an extra layer of encryption and anonymity.
items.howTo: Connect to a no-logs VPN service first, then launch Tor Browser. Choose VPN providers that accept anonymous payments.

items.task: Use Tor on a separate OS or virtual machine
items.why: Isolates Tor activities from your main system and prevents data leaks from other applications.
items.howTo: Consider using Tails OS, or set up a dedicated VM with Linux for Tor browsing. Never use Tor on your main OS with other apps running.

items.task: Verify no DNS leaks are occurring
items.why: DNS leaks can reveal your browsing activity and real IP address despite using Tor.
items.howTo: Visit DNS leak test sites through Tor to verify your DNS queries are properly routed. Results should show Tor exit node location.

items.task: Ensure system clock is accurate
items.why: Incorrect time can prevent Tor from connecting properly and may fingerprint your system.
items.howTo: Enable automatic time sync on your OS. Verify time zone matches your claimed location if using VPN.

items.task: Configure firewall to only allow Tor traffic
items.why: Prevents other applications from bypassing Tor and leaking your real IP address.
items.howTo: Set up firewall rules to block all traffic except through Tor ports (9001, 9030, 9050, 9051). Block direct internet access for other apps.

items.task: Disable or physically block camera and microphone
items.why: Prevents potential malware from accessing audio/video without your knowledge.
items.howTo: Disable camera/microphone in system settings, use physical covers, or disconnect USB devices when using Tor.

items.task: Verify.onion links from trusted sources only
items.why: Malicious.onion sites can host malware, scams, or law enforcement honeypots.
items.howTo: Use established directories like The Hidden Wiki, cross-reference links from multiple sources, never click random links.

items.task: Monitor and avoid malicious exit nodes
items.why: Some exit nodes are operated by malicious actors who monitor traffic and inject malware.
items.howTo: Check your exit node location regularly, use 'New Identity' if you notice suspicious behavior or repeated bad exit nodes.

items.task: Use privacy-focused cryptocurrencies for transactions
items.why: Bitcoin transactions can be traced; privacy coins provide better anonymity for dark web purchases.
items.howTo: Use Monero, Zcash, or other privacy coins. Never use exchanges that require KYC verification. Use coin mixing services.

items.task: Set up PGP encryption for communications
items.why: Encrypts messages end-to-end, protecting communications even if intercepted by authorities.
items.howTo: Generate PGP key pair using GPG, share public key safely, encrypt all sensitive communications before sending.

items.task: Research marketplace reputation and escrow systems
items.why: Many dark web marketplaces are scams or honeypots designed to steal money or identify users.
items.howTo: Read forum reviews, check marketplace uptime history, always use escrow services, start with small test purchases.

items.task: Understand legal implications in your jurisdiction
items.why: Laws regarding Tor usage and dark web access vary significantly between countries.
items.howTo: Research local laws about Tor usage, encryption, and online anonymity. Consider legal risks before accessing certain content.

pro_tips: Always assume you're being monitored - practice perfect operational security even for legal activities on Tor.
Use a privacy-focused browser for regular privacy needs and reserve Tor only for situations requiring maximum anonymity.
Never mix Tor activities with your real identity - create completely separate digital personas and never cross-contaminate them.
Test your setup regularly using online anonymity checkers to ensure no information is leaking about your real identity.
Keep detailed notes about your security practices in an encrypted journal to maintain consistency and identify potential weaknesses.
